newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED PEN PICTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED PEN PICTURES.

text.p: Pen pictures of players most likely to play for Manchester United in Sunday's English F.A. Cup third round tie against Tottenham Hotspur:
Peter Schmeichel. Goalkeeper, Age 33. Despite occasional histrionics, arguably the world's best goalkeeper. Giant and imposing.
Denis Irwin. Right-back, 31. Reliable, consistent Republic of Ireland full-back who has played more than 300 games since joining United from Oldham in June 1990.
Gary Pallister. Central defender, 31. Now recovered from the back injury which kept him out of Euro 96. Commanding and reassuring and a major threat at set-pieces.

Gary Neville. Defender, 21. Reliable and fast. Gary and Philip Neville became the first brothers since Bobby and Jack Charlton to play in the same England side when they appeared against China in May.
David May. Central defender, 26. Has established himself as a first team player this season following the departure of Steve Bruce. Enjoying his best season at Old Trafford.

David Beckham. Midfielder, 21. Scored an extraordinary goal from his own half against Wimbledon in August, which secured his call-up to the England team. Has made an outstanding start to the season, scoring stunning recent goals at West Ham and Nottingham Forest.
Karel Poborsky. Midfielder, 23. Best known for his superb goal for the Czech Republic against Portugal during Euro 96. Has failed to secure a first team place in his first season at Old Trafford.
Roy Keane. Midfielder, 25. Now recovered from injury, his aggression gives United plenty of drive and strength in midfield. Prone to losing his temper.
Nicky Butt. Midfielder, 21. Rock-hard, industrious and committed, lost his place with the arrival of Poborsky and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer but has since won it back again.

Ryan Giggs. Left wing, 23. Doubts are beginning to creep in about his potential. Still capable of winning a game with devastating ball control and speed, the most naturally-gifted player in Britain needs to assert himself more now he's no longer a novice. Even so, United sorely missed him on the left flank when he was sidelined through injury in November.

Eric Cantona. Striker, 30. England's Player of the Year. An inspiration for United since returning to the team after being banned in 1995 for attacking a spectator, but has had, by his own admission, a mediocre season so far. Scored the winning goal in the Cup final against Liverpool which secured United's double. Iconoclastic, with a notorious temper. His French international career seems to be over.
Paul Scholes. Striker, 22. One of the "Ferguson babes". In and out of the side this season, but a proven scorer.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Striker, 23. Joined United in the summer as a long-term investment from Norwegian club Molde and made a huge initial impact with a number of well-taken goals. Less impressive recently but still a first team regular. Nicknamed by the fans, "the baby-faced killer", Cantona said he reminded him of French striker Jean-Pierre Papin.

Jordi Cruyff. Forward, 22. Son of Johan, he moved to United from Barcelona after Euro 96. Like Poborsky, has not established himself in the starting lineup despite a couple of bright early-season performances.
Brian McClair. Forward, 33. Used mainly as provider behind the front men. Highly respected by Alex Ferguson for his graft and effective linkplay.

Andy Cole. Forward, 25. Has never recaptured the predatory instinct he showed at Newcastle two seasons ago before his 7.0 million pound ($12 million) transfer to Old Trafford. On the bench for much of last season and sidelined recently with a cracked bone in his leg. Made his comeback appearance as a substitute at Nottingham Forest on December 26, scoring in United's 4-0 win.
